questions.question: The earliest morphological change of reversible cell injury is:
questions.explanation: Failure of the Na⁺/K⁺ pump causes influx of water; nuclear changes (pyknosis, karyorrhexis, karyolysis) indicate irreversible necrosis.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Coagulative necrosis is characteristic of infarction of:

options.B: Solid organs such as the heart, kidney and spleen

questions.explanation: Brain infarcts show liquefactive necrosis; TB shows caseous necrosis; fat necrosis occurs in the pancreas and breast.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Caseous necrosis is typically seen in:
questions.explanation: Cheesy white appearance with granulomatous inflammation.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which statement about apoptosis is correct?

options.B: It is a form of necrosis
options.D: It is an energy-dependent programmed cell death without inflammation

questions.explanation: Caspases mediate apoptosis; chromatin condensation and apoptotic bodies are features.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Dry gangrene is typically caused by:

options.D: Arterial occlusion, as in diabetes or atherosclerosis

questions.explanation: Wet gangrene has superadded infection with putrefaction.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The predominant cell type in acute inflammation is the:
questions.explanation: Macrophages and lymphocytes dominate chronic inflammation.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the five cardinal signs of inflammation?
questions.explanation: Rubor, calor, tumor, dolor and loss of function.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which substance is a potent chemotactic agent for neutrophils?
questions.explanation: Histamine and bradykinin increase vascular permeability.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A granuloma is a collection of:

options.D: Activated macrophages (epithelioid cells), often with giant cells and lymphocytes

questions.explanation: Seen in TB, sarcoidosis, leprosy and Crohn's disease.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Langhans' giant cells, with nuclei arranged in a horseshoe pattern at the periphery, are typical of:
questions.explanation: Foreign body giant cells have randomly scattered nuclei.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In the proliferative phase of wound healing, collagen is synthesised mainly by:
questions.explanation: Type III collagen is replaced by type I collagen during remodelling.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Virchow's triad of thrombosis consists of:

options.B: Endothelial injury, stasis or turbulence of blood flow, and hypercoagulability

questions.explanation: Arterial thrombi mainly result from endothelial injury; venous thrombi from stasis.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most common source of pulmonary embolism is:

options.D: Deep veins of the lower limb

questions.explanation: Deep vein thrombosis of the calf or iliofemoral veins.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Infarcts of the lung, intestine and liver are typically:
questions.explanation: Pale infarcts occur in solid organs with end-arterial supply: heart, kidney, spleen.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Oedema due to hypoalbuminaemia is caused by:
questions.explanation: Seen in nephrotic syndrome, cirrhosis and malnutrition.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which feature favours a malignant tumour?

options.C: Invasion of surrounding tissue and metastasis

questions.explanation: Anaplasia, high mitotic rate and invasion characterise malignancy.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Carcinomas typically spread first by the:
questions.explanation: Sarcomas typically spread haematogenously.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Alpha-fetoprotein is a tumour marker for:

options.D: Hepatocellular carcinoma and yolk sac tumours

questions.explanation: PSA: prostate; CEA: colorectal; CA-125: ovarian.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Aflatoxin B1 is associated with:
questions.explanation: Produced by Aspergillus flavus on stored grains; also hepatitis B.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which of the following is a tumour-suppressor gene?
questions.explanation: p53 is the ‘guardian of the genome’; mutated in over 50% of human cancers.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Type I (immediate) hypersensitivity is mediated by:
questions.explanation: Anaphylaxis, asthma and hay fever; type IV is delayed (tuberculin test).
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The tuberculin (Mantoux) test is an example of:
questions.explanation: Read at 48–72 hours; induration of ≥10 mm is positive.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The immunoglobulin that crosses the placenta is:
questions.explanation: IgM is the first antibody produced in a primary response; IgA is in secretions.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which autoantibody is characteristic of Hashimoto's thyroiditis?
questions.explanation: Anti-dsDNA is characteristic of SLE.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Down syndrome is most commonly due to:
questions.explanation: Associated with advanced maternal age, congenital heart disease (AV canal defect) and early Alzheimer's.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The karyotype in Turner syndrome is:
questions.explanation: Short stature, webbed neck, primary amenorrhoea. Klinefelter is 47,XXY.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is inherited as:
questions.explanation: Mutation in the dystrophin gene on Xp21; serum CK is markedly raised.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Sickle cell anaemia is inherited as:
questions.explanation: Heterozygotes (sickle trait) are usually asymptomatic and protected against malaria.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The earliest lesion of atherosclerosis is the:
questions.explanation: Lipid-laden foam cells in the intima.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The characteristic lesion of rheumatic carditis is the:
questions.explanation: Aschoff bodies contain Anitschkow cells (caterpillar cells).
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Emphysema is defined as:

options.D: Permanent enlargement of airspaces distal to the terminal bronchiole with destruction of walls

questions.explanation: Centriacinar emphysema is associated with smoking; panacinar with alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which lung cancer is MOST strongly related to smoking and arises centrally?

options.B: Squamous cell carcinoma and small cell carcinoma

questions.explanation: Adenocarcinoma is the most common type overall and arises peripherally.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In osteoporosis the bone shows:

options.C: Reduced bone mass with normal mineral content per unit of bone

questions.explanation: Osteomalacia is defective mineralisation; Paget's is disorganised remodelling.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In rheumatoid arthritis, the destruction of articular cartilage is caused by:
questions.explanation: Rheumatoid nodules occur in subcutaneous tissue; fibrinoid necrosis surrounded by palisading histiocytes.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Staphylococcus aureus is a:

options.D: Gram-positive coccus in clusters, coagulase positive

questions.explanation: Streptococci form chains; Staph aureus causes boils, osteomyelitis and food poisoning.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The standard method for sterilising surgical instruments is:
questions.explanation: Hot air oven at 160 °C for 1 hour is used for glassware and powders.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Mycobacterium tuberculosis is identified by:
questions.explanation: Mycolic acid in the cell wall resists decolourisation by acid.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which hepatitis virus is a DNA virus?
questions.explanation: HAV, HCV and HEV are RNA viruses; HBV is a partially double-stranded DNA virus.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: HIV infects mainly cells bearing the receptor:
questions.explanation: Helper T-cell depletion leads to opportunistic infections.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Poliovirus belongs to which group?
questions.explanation: Faecal–oral transmission; oral vaccine (Sabin) is a live attenuated vaccine.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Tetanospasmin acts by blocking release of:

options.D: Inhibitory neurotransmitters (glycine and GABA) in the spinal cord

questions.explanation: Botulinum toxin blocks acetylcholine release, causing flaccid paralysis.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The cause of malignant tertian malaria is:
questions.explanation: Falciparum causes cerebral malaria and has no relapse; vivax can relapse from hypnozoites.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The Widal test is used for diagnosis of:
questions.explanation: Detects agglutinins against O and H antigens; blood culture is best in the first week.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
